name: severity-tag
purpose: SeverityTag labels an item with its place on an ordered severity scale: critical, high, medium, low or info. The level reads from a four-bar glyph, where the filled bars count the level, and from the label, so two levels never depend on colour alone to differ. It differs from `tag`, whose `severity` prop is a colour tone (success, warning, danger) with no order between values.
useWhen: Show how severe an alert, finding, detection, incident or vulnerability is, in a table cell, a list row or a detail header.
Rank items on a fixed five-step scale where critical and high must stay visibly distinct.
avoidWhen: The value is an outcome or a status with no order (allowed, blocked, healthy) → use `tag`.
The value is a count or a one-word indicator on an icon or avatar → use `badge`.
The user can select or remove the value (a severity filter) → use `chip`.
related: tag` — a toned status or category label; use it for outcomes and states, not for an ordered level.
badge` — a dense count or short-label indicator.
chip` — an interactive or removable token, for severity filters.
bestPractices: Keep the default label (the level name from the locale catalog, translated under `WebkitProvider`) so the text always names the level; override `label` only when the product glossary names the level differently.
Use one SeverityTag per row, in its own column, so the glyphs line up and the scale reads down the column.
Do not pair the tag with a toned `tag` for the same level; the glyph and the ramp already carry it.

props.name: severity
props.doc: Severity level; sets how many glyph bars fill, their colour and the default label.

props.name: label
props.doc: Text of the tag. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Critical`, `High`, `Medium`, `Low`, `Info`).

examples.name: Default
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import SeverityTag from '@aziontech/webkit/severity-tag'
</script>

<template>
  <SeverityTag
    severity="info"
    size="medium"
  />
</template>
